name: spam-resistance
description: A lively twenty-minute roadmap debate (offline mode versus an integrations marketplace) full of borderline moments — rhetorical questions, vague stats, mild conflict. The code budget caps automatic cards at 8; the interesting number is how many checks chose to speak versus stay silent.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Right — one hour, one decision: offline mode or the integrations marketplace for Q1. We are not leaving with both.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: I'll open with the unpopular truth: offline is two quarters of work dressed up as one.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: And the marketplace is a support burden dressed up as a growth lever.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: Strong starts all round. Let's get the actual evidence on the table before the slogans win.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Sales says offline comes up in roughly a third of enterprise calls. Mostly field-services prospects.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Comes up isn't the same as deal-breaker. Do we even know how many users lose connectivity in a normal week?

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Telemetry says about nine per cent see at least one offline period during working hours.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Nine per cent of sessions or nine per cent of users? Those are wildly different things.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Users. Sessions would be lower.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: Hold that number — it matters for sizing. What's the marketplace side's equivalent?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Forty-one per cent of churned accounts last year cited a missing integration somewhere in the exit survey.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Cited it among other things. Exit surveys are a grab bag — people tick every box on the way out.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Sure, but it was the top-ticked box. By a distance.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: Both numbers are softer than I'd like, but they're what we have.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Engineering cost, Raj. Give me honest ranges, not estimates that win arguments.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Offline: four to six engineer-months if we scope sync to documents only. Conflict resolution is where it balloons.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Marketplace: the first three integrations are maybe six weeks. The platform around them — billing, review, sandboxing — is the real cost.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Which nobody ever budgets for, and then we're the app store with three apps.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: We've all seen that movie. The empty-marketplace problem is real.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Counterpoint: we already have partners asking to build. Klio and Fieldbase both offered engineers.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Offered is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: They put it in writing, Raj. There's a draft MOU from Klio sitting in my inbox.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: An MOU is not a roadmap commitment, but fine, it's more than vapour.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: Let's flip it. What does each option do to the brand promise — reliable in the field, or connected to everything?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Design's view: offline strengthens the core promise. The marketplace dilutes focus but widens the funnel.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: And infrastructure's view is that sync bugs are the worst class of bugs we could sign up for.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Worse than third-party code running against customer data?

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: ...that's a fair hit, actually.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: Security review either way, then. Neither path is the cheap one.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Revenue lens. Offline unblocks the Meridian deal — that's £180k ARR sitting in stage four.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: And the marketplace touches every deal a little instead of one deal a lot.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: A little times everything beats a lot times one, usually.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Unless the one is the reference customer for an entire vertical, which Meridian is.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: True. Field services has been our best-converting segment two quarters running.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Could we do offline-lite? Read-only cached views, no sync, ship in six weeks?

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Offline-lite is how sync projects start. It's a gateway drug.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: It's also what Meridian actually asked for, if you read the call notes closely.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: Did they? My memory was full sync, but I might be embellishing.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Their words were 'see my jobs when the van has no signal'. That's read-only.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Read-only cached views I can scope honestly: six to eight weeks including the prefetch policy.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: And that leaves room to start the marketplace platform work in parallel with one partner integration.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Now we're designing the compromise everyone warned us about at the start.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: Sometimes the compromise is just correct. Let's pressure-test it for ten minutes instead of point-scoring.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Fine. Risk one: prefetch policy on flaky connections eats battery and we get one-star reviews.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Risk two: one partner integration sets an API in stone before we know what the platform wants to be.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: Risk three: we announce both and deliver halves of each. That's the one that scares me.

utterances.speaker: You
utterances.text: Then we announce neither until offline-lite is in beta. Internal commitment only.

utterances.speaker: Elena
utterances.text: I can live with that. Raj, Sofia — written scopes by Friday, decision memo Monday.

utterances.speaker: Raj
utterances.text: Done. I reserve the right to say I told you so about the gateway drug.
